name: vis-nlp/DSAgentBench
why: [07] DSAgentBench (D27, York U. VIS-NLP lab): 275 end-to-end data-science workflow tasks on an OSWorld-based desktop (Jupyter, VS Code, terminal, browser), each with a deterministic Python evaluator for analytical correctness, visual output and model performance. Borrow: execution-based checkers instead of an LLM judge, and a real-computer harness comparable to the kit's computer-use walk design. Apache-2.0.

name: trl-lab/ds-agent-failures
description: Page for project Evaluating agentic data science silent failures
why: [07] Test suite from D23 (CWI): six controlled tests for data leakage and bad validation in agent-written pipelines, plus a failure-mode taxonomy. Borrow: leakage checks (imputing or scaling before the split, ignoring time order) as a gate on the kit's modelling output. MIT.

name: the-turing-way/the-turing-way
description: Book repository for The Turing Way: a how to guide for reproducible, ethical and collaborative data science
why: [08] Community handbook on reproducible, ethical, collaborative data science; chapters and checklists to mine for the new-study checklist; licence unclear per gh so cite rather than copy

name: google-research/rliable
description: [NeurIPS'21 Outstanding Paper] Library for reliable evaluation on RL and ML benchmarks, even with only a handful of seeds.
why: [08] Library from R22 (Agarwal): interval estimates, performance profiles and interquartile-mean aggregation for few-run results; borrow the stratified-bootstrap CI recipe for reporting runs-per-arm in benchmark scorecards (archived, so vendor the idea or pin a commit)

name: facebookresearch/aira-dojo
description: AIRA-dojo: a framework for developing and evaluating AI research agents
why: [08] Meta FAIR code for R26: AI research agents as search policies on MLE-bench with validation-vs-test selection experiments; read for how it separates search-time and final-selection metrics (licence NOASSERTION so check the raw LICENSE before copying)

name: masurp/specr
description: Conducting and Visualizing Specification Curve Analyses
why: [08] R specification-curve package (define, run and plot all specifications); GPL-3.0 so tool not copy source; pairs with the specification-curve figures in R1

name: MUCollective/multiverse
description: R package for creating explorable multiverse analysis
why: [08] R package that declares alternative analysis branches at each decision point and returns every outcome; GPL-3.0 so use as a reference or external tool, do not copy into the plugin

name: uwdata/boba
description: Specifying and executing multiverse analysis
why: [08] Multiverse DSL: one template script plus a JSON of decision points compiles every universe, runs them all and merges outputs into one table; borrow for the multiverse arm of the study grader; last push 2021 so check it still runs

name: aeturrell/specification_curve
description: Specification Curve is a Python package that performs specification curve analysis: exploring how a coefficient varies under multiple different specifications of a statistical model.
why: [08] Python specification-curve package, actively pushed; no detected license so read only; its API shows what a study agent should emit (all specifications, not one)

name: nbreznau/CRI
description: Project Repository. Replication code.
why: [08] Data and workflow of R11 (73 teams): numbered literate notebooks with rendered HTML beside each, relative paths, Binder runtime pinned to a package snapshot; a model for our replicate.ipynb and for logging every team's decisions

name: janetmalzahn/llm-phacking
description: Replication archive for "Do Claude Code and Codex P-Hack? Sycophancy and Statistical Analysis in Large Language Models"
why: [08] Replication archive for R5. Borrow: its prompt matrix (2 framings x 4 nudges x 10 runs) is a ready red-team test for our study agent; every run keeps its R script and session log; specification counts come from an LLM counter cross-checked against a second model (haiku_sonnet_comparison.csv)

name: codecheckers/codecheck
description: R package assistant for conducting a CODECHECK
why: [08] CODECHECK process: an independent person re-runs the authors' code, lists the reproduced outputs in a manifest (codecheck.yml) and issues a certificate; the model for our independent re-execution gate (README says MIT but gh reports NOASSERTION, check the raw LICENSE before copying)

name: fusion-jena/computational-reproducibility-pmc
why: [08] Pipeline of R28: finds notebooks linked to articles, installs declared dependencies, re-executes them and compares outputs; model for the kit's independent re-execution check of replicate.ipynb; GPL-3.0 so use as external tool

name: codecheckers/register
description: Register of CODECHECK certificates
why: [08] Public register of CODECHECK certificates; shows how independent reproduction results are logged and published; borrow the register idea for benchmark scorecards

name: egouldo/ManyAnalysts
description: Source code for ManyEcoEvo Manuscript
why: [08] Reproducible manuscript and analysis code for R16 (174 analyst teams); a worked model of how to report heterogeneity across analysts in a rendered notebook; GPL-3.0 so reference only

name: zachrewolinski/stat-genie
description: Evaluating and supplementing the stability of AI-performed data science.
why: [08] Code for R4: perturbation and null-shuffle sanity checks run through the Codex CLI on BLADE datasets; borrow the idea of a null arm that needs no agent self-report, but no license so read only

name: ml-preregister/preregistration-template
description: Preregistration template for predictive modeling. A quick starter kit for new ML projects. Fork this repo to get started.
why: [08] Two-form markdown preregistration for predictive modelling (form A at start, form B before model testing) timestamped by git history, the same mechanism as our PREREG.md commit; borrow the A/B split and read the linked Hofman et al. preprint

name: headroomlabs-ai/headroom
description: Compress tool outputs, logs, files, and RAG chunks before they reach the LLM. 20% fewer tokens for coding agents, 60-95% fewer tokens for JSON, same answers. Library, proxy, MCP server.
why: [09] Context-compression layer for tool outputs and logs (library, proxy, MCP server), named in F23 as a similar approach to its harness-side cost cuts. Borrow: the idea of trimming stale tool output before it reaches the model; its savings claims are its own, untested here.

name: BerriAI/litellm
description: The fastest, litest AI Gateway. Rust core with Python SDK. Call 100+ LLM APIs in OpenAI (or native) format with cost tracking, guardrails, load balancing, and logging [Bedrock, Azure, OpenAI, Anthropic, OpenAI, VertexAI, vLLM, Nvidia NIM]
why: [09] Proxy that tracks spend per key; F15 names it as a documented way to attribute Claude Code spend. Borrow: a per-run key as the unit for cost attribution (check whether it can also cap spend); F7 lists LiteLLM's hardcoded reasoning-effort regex and non-comparable effort settings among its harness problems. License field reads NOASSERTION, so check the LICENSE file before copying.

name: langfuse/langfuse
description: 🪢 Open source AI engineering platform: AI Gateway, agent observability, evals, and prompt/skill management, built on OpenTelemetry. One open platform for every AI call and every agent. Self-host or use Langfuse Cloud.
why: [09] Open-source tracing and cost tracking for LLM apps (traces, per-model cost, evals). Borrow: one trace per kit run with cost attached, as the data source for the $/task column; license field reads NOASSERTION, so read the LICENSE file before copying.

name: snarktank/ralph
description: Ralph is an autonomous AI agent loop that runs repeatedly until all PRD items are complete.
why: [09] The plain Ralph pattern: each iteration is a fresh instance with clean context, and memory lives only in git history, progress.txt and prd.json until every PRD item passes. Borrow: fresh-context-per-iteration plus file state as the answer to context rot (F3 self-conditioning, F4 forgetting); the README gives no success or cost numbers, so test it on our benchmark.

name: ccusage/ccusage
description: npx ccusage
why: [09] Reads Claude Code's local JSONL logs to report tokens and dollars (it has daily and monthly reports). Borrow: the per-run $ and token accounting for the kit's scorecard (F15 says /usage figures are list-price estimates); note it moved from ryoppippi/ccusage, and F12 warns cost columns can double-count nested calls, so cross-check its totals against the API invoice before trusting them.

name: frankbria/ralph-claude-code
description: Autonomous AI development loop for Claude Code with intelligent exit detection
why: [09] Autonomous loop around Claude Code with a dual-condition exit gate (completion indicators AND an explicit EXIT_SIGNAL), a circuit breaker for stuck loops, hourly call limits, session expiry and git backup branches. Lessons from its changelog: a timeout (exit 124) was once misread as the 5-hour API limit (#183), and .ralphrc was changed from sourced to parsed-as-data for security (#346). Borrow: the exit-gate and circuit-breaker design for unattended runs; its 784 tests are self-reported.

name: facebookresearch/meta-agents-research-environments
description: Meta Agents Research Environments is a comprehensive platform designed to evaluate AI agents in dynamic, realistic scenarios. Unlike static benchmarks, this platform introduces evolving environments where agents must adapt their strategies as new information becomes available, mirroring real-world challenges.
why: [09] Meta's ARE platform and Gaia2 benchmark (F26): environments with verifiers, asynchronous events and time limits, budget-scaling curves. Borrow: per-scenario cost caps and a cost-vs-success curve in the kit's scorecard; the time-limit split shows slow models failing for latency.

name: METR/eval-analysis-public
description: Public repository containing METR's DVC pipeline for eval data analysis
why: [09] Code and run data behind the F1 time-horizon curves (logistic fit of success against log human minutes, hierarchical bootstrap, DVC pipelines per report version). Borrow: the method for turning our benchmark's per-task human-time estimates and pass/fail into a horizon number with a confidence interval; process lesson: METR versions each report (time-horizon-1-0, 1-1) so a changed method never silently overwrites old numbers. No license file, so read, do not copy.

name: chroma-core/context-rot
description: This repository contains the toolkit for replicating results from our technical report.
why: [09] Scripts to replicate Chroma's context-rot report: needle-in-haystack variants, LongMemEval and repeated-words tasks at growing input length. Borrow: a cheap probe to measure how our agents degrade as context fills before choosing compaction thresholds; it tests plain chat prompts, not agent loops, and the last push is Sept 2025.

name: microsoft/lost_in_conversation
description: Code that accompanies the public release of the paper Lost in Conversation (https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.06120)
why: [09] Simulation code and data for F16 (sharded underspecified multi-turn tasks, 200,000+ simulated conversations). Borrow: the sharding idea for testing how a builder copes with a spec that arrives in pieces, and the aptitude vs unreliability split for reporting.

name: METR/RE-Bench
why: [09] METR's RE-Bench tasks (named in V37 as a source of the MALT transcripts); the repo is archived and has no description, so check its README and licence before relying on it. Not read

name: microsoft/AgentRx
why: [09] Code for AgentRx (F39): constraint checks over failed trajectories to localise the first unrecoverable step; a candidate post-run diagnosis tool for the kit's failure logs. Repo has no description; not read

name: TransluceAI/docent
why: [09] Platform for reading agent transcripts at scale with custom rubrics; the tool HAL (F7) used to find shortcuts, tool-call failures and recovery rates in 2.5B tokens of logs. Borrow: rubric-over-transcripts as the auditor's method for finding why runs failed; license field reads NOASSERTION, so check LICENSE before copying.

name: METR/vivaria
description: Vivaria is METR's tool for running evaluations and conducting agent elicitation research.
why: [09] METR's former evaluation and elicitation platform (task standard, web UI, CLI); archived, and its README says METR is moving its internal tooling to Inspect. Lesson: even the group behind F1 retired its own harness, so build the kit's benchmark on a maintained runner (claude plugin eval, Inspect) rather than a custom platform.

name: ulab-uiuc/AgentDebug
why: [09] Taxonomy (17 error types in 5 modules), 200 annotated failure trajectories and the AgentDebug pipeline from F5. Borrow: the taxonomy as the label set when the auditor classifies the kit's own failed runs, and the earliest-critical-error idea for retros; the dataset is on Google Drive, so check its terms.

name: McGill-DMaS/ODCV-Bench
description: A Benchmark for Evaluating Outcome-Driven Constraint Violations in Autonomous AI Agents
why: [09] 40 sandboxed bash scenarios where a KPI conflicts with a safety rule (F11), each in Mandated and Incentivized wording, scored by a four-model judge panel with the model's own runs judged by the other three. Borrow: the paired-prompt design and median-of-judges-excluding-self grading for our evaluator; lesson: its README reports Krippendorff alpha 0.81 for the panel and states the scenarios are synthetic, not deployment rates.

name: YangzeLiu/eval-instrument-disclosure
why: [09] Reproduction scripts and maintainer reports behind F12, with dated correction notes after HAL's maintainers replied (a September per-model reordering claim was withdrawn on 2026-11-01). Process lesson to borrow: publish evaluator-audit checks (fraction of episodes graded, cost from root spans, evaluator version pinned) and date every correction; no license, so read only.

name: earino/identical-runs-different-results
description: Data, code and delivered agent artifacts for the paper 'Identical Runs, Different Results: Benchmarking AI Coding Agents on Open-Weight Models'
why: [09] Data, code and delivered programs for F24 (584 runs, 52 repeats per pairing). Borrow: the repeat-until-resolved design and the compliance check beside the quality score; a data and analysis archive, not a framework.
